title: SR-1.26 One write can never make the vault unopenable
request: Closes G91: writing notes/a.md and then notes/a.md/b.md is accepted by checkPath, the second put is appended to the op log and fdatasynced (src/engine/vault.mjs:226) before mkdirSync throws EEXIST (:235), and every later Vault.open() throws EEXIST from recover() (:119, called unguarded at :66), even after the file is deleted by hand, because recover() first rebuilds it. The daemon, the doctor, compact and the runner can never open the vault again. Any token with write scope over a matching path reaches it (MCP memev_write and memev_append, HTTP PUT and PATCH, the tunnel when remote access is on): a remote denial of service on the vault. Found by the SR-1.22 red-team round and reproduced on 31 October 2026 at main be457db. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-0.03, QL-1.02. Lands ahead of the SR-1 queue. Sensitive path (the oplog and the vault): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge.

tasks.title: No path under a note and no note over a folder is ever logged
requirements: write, append and every other logging entry point refuse, before anything is appended to the log, a path one of whose parent segments is an existing note, and a path that names an existing folder of notes; the refusal names the conflicting path
the refusal reaches every caller as a 4xx with that reason (MCP tools and HTTP PUT and PATCH), never a 500, and the log, the files and the recall index are unchanged by it
the check runs on the materialised view of the log, so a path that exists only in the log (a file deleted by hand) still conflicts

every logging entry point (write, append, remember, checkpoint, journal and the external-import path) asks the file system first: it creates the parent folders and writes the temporary file, and appends to the log only when that succeeded; a failure there refuses the operation with nothing logged; the rename after the append is the only step that can fail after logging, and SR-1.22, which builds on this contract, completes it from the log; until SR-1.22 lands, that one window keeps the behaviour of G87

the path rules of this requirement apply to every path a call would create (write, append, remember, checkpoint, journal and the external import): a NUL byte, any other C0 control character or DEL; a segment longer than 255 UTF-8 bytes or a path longer than 1024 UTF-8 bytes; a segment ending in a dot or a space; a parent segment ending in a note extension, matched without regard to case; and a path whose fold key (per segment: NFC, then toUpperCase(), then toLowerCase()) equals an existing live head, or one of its parent folders, under a different spelling, so a vault moved between Linux, macOS and Windows cannot hold two names one file system sees as one; get, delete, review, why and provenance accept every path the log already holds
delete removes the folders it leaves empty up to the vault root, so a later write of a note with that folder's name is not refused by an empty folder
the task adds its helpers in new files under test/helpers/ and changes no existing helper, which 123 test files share
a target that exists on disk as a folder, whether or not it holds notes, or as anything other than a regular file, is refused before anything is logged, naming the target; no temporary file is left
a conflict refusal is a VaultError with code conflict and a field conflict naming the other path; HTTP answers 409 with that field in its JSON body, and the MCP text starts with 'conflict:'

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/vault-path-conflict.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

tasks.title: A vault that already holds such a record opens
requirements: recover() handles each path on its own: a path that cannot be materialised is skipped with its reason recorded (a skipped list the doctor shows; SR-1.21 also surfaces it), and recovery continues with the other paths; Vault.open() never throws because of one path

a vault whose log already holds the conflicting put written by the code at be457db opens, every other note reads its logged body, and memev doctor reports the conflicting path with the command that resolves it
nothing is appended to the log by recovery

per-path recovery covers recover(), rebuildInto and _importExternal: each handles every error class on one path (EEXIST, ENOTDIR, EISDIR, ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE, ENAMETOOLONG and any other), records the path, and continues; a test drives at least three error classes through each
a skipped head is marked unrecoverable in memory and is never turned into an external delete by syncFromDisk, a pull or the doctor's fix; writes to the good side of a conflict keep working
the walk loop of recover() and rebuildInto skip a symlink (dangling or to a folder) and any entry that cannot be read, recording its reason; a link is never followed out of the vault
T1's conflict check counts a head that recovery skipped as absent, so the good side of an existing conflict stays writable before any resolving command

the resolving command is memev doctor --resolve <path>: it logs a put of the skipped note's body at a free path the doctor names, then a delete of the old head, so the note stays listed, readable and searchable
the fixture's .memev files are committed with git add -f, so a clean clone holds the fixture vault
